surge.text: Uber splits every city into small hexagons.
In each one, it compares riders asking with drivers free.
More riders than drivers? The price surges.
Higher prices pull more drivers in, and it settles.

gaming.text: But a price set by supply can be gamed.
Drivers at some airports went offline together.
No cars on the map, so the price surged.
Then they came back online and took surge fares.
That's artificial scarcity: a fake shortage, a real price.
gaming.say: That's artificial scarcity. A fake shortage, a real price.

smooth.text: Fix one: never price from a single snapshot.
Average supply over minutes and nearby hexagons.
A sudden dip barely moves the price.

fixes.text: Fix two: flag many drivers going offline at once, in one place.
Fix three: lock the rider's price when they request.
Fix four: forecast demand and send drivers early.

pipeline.text: Under the hood, every driver's location streams in every few seconds.
A stream processor counts riders and drivers per hexagon.
The pricing service turns those counts into the price you see.
